attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own post, stated in his voice.

semantics.note: 'Is not going to' is a firm forecast with no hedge and no deadline. The normalised proposition matches the statement.

contract.note: Reading 'movies' as feature-length films made mainly with Sora is a fair, ordinary reading given the context about replacing film-making. Settling early on discontinuation is reasonable: a withdrawn tool cannot go on to generate movies. The result does depend on that reading and on that rule.

evidence.note: OpenAI's dated notice (2026-03-24) that Sora 2 models and the Videos API would be removed on 2026-09-24, with no replacement. This is a company disclosure, but it is the announcement the rule calls for.
TechCrunch reported the same day that OpenAI was shutting down the Sora product.
Dated May 2026: the leading Sora-based feature, Critterz, was human-led and AI-assisted and missed its premiere after the shutdown. No Sora-made feature had been released.
The Sora 2 model was still in ChatGPT on the announcement day. This makes the withdrawal look less complete, but the rule only needs the product shutdown and API removal to be announced.

reviews.rationale: The early-resolution rule is met by dated events. On 2026-03-24 OpenAI announced the Sora product shutdown and the removal of Sora 2 from the API with no replacement. No feature-length film made mainly with Sora had been released by then, or later in the packet. ChatGPT access (e4) and a possible 2027 Critterz release are caveats. Critterz is human-led, though, so it would not count under the contract.

attribution.note: Zitron's own assertion in his own post.

semantics.note: A present-tense, unhedged claim about the state of the three problems when he posted. All three problems are kept.

contract.note: The plain reading (each problem still large and unresolved, with no fix near deployment) is fair and ordinary. A target period running up to the post date suits a present-tense claim. 'Not close' has no measure, so the reading decides the result.

evidence.note: Stanford preprint, January 2024: legal hallucination rates of 69–88% in leading models. It covers only the legal domain and slightly older models.
IEA projection reported January 2024: data-centre electricity demand, driven partly by AI, could double by 2026.
Reuters, January 2024: Altman said AI needs an energy breakthrough that has not yet happened. This is a third party's statement, not an independent measurement.
WSJ via Tom's Hardware, October 2023: Copilot lost more than $20 per user per month. It rests on one anonymous source and one product.
The IEA expected clean supply to meet the new demand. That is about supply and emissions, not the size of AI's energy needs.

reviews.rationale: In-period evidence fits all three parts. Hallucination rates stayed high in a large independent test. AI-driven electricity demand was projected to grow, and OpenAI's CEO said a breakthrough was needed. A flagship generative AI product reportedly cost more to serve than it earned. Nothing in the packet shows any of the three was near solved. The profitability evidence is thin: one anonymous report.
